description: Kindle Paperwhite 4 (10th generation, i.MX6SLL, device tree) on stock firmware 5.18.1.1.1: the stock kernel the handoff module loads into, and the physical plan of the jump. DRAFT: not run on a device
supported_zh: Kindle Paperwhite 4（第 10 代，2018 年款），固件 5.18.1.1.1
compatible_why: a device-tree boot has no machine number (__machine_arch_type is ~0); the SoC compatible is what the stock tree's root node and the next kernel's DT_MACHINE_START both name
identity_limit_why: 2G/2G: PAGE_OFFSET == PHYS_OFFSET == 0x80000000, so the kernel's lowmem is one to one up to the end of the 512 MiB of RAM; the private table clears only the user half below the module area (0x7f000000) and copies the rest (handoff/private-table.h)
cmdline_base: consoleblank=0 uart_at_4m quiet secure_cpu=1 androidboot.secure_cpu=1 androidboot.prod=1 androidboot.unlocked_kernel=false panic=5 softlockup_panic=1 hung_task_panic=1 initcall_debug
cmdline_base_why: The stock command line without root=, rootwait and console= (dd_fdt in boot/devicedata requires exactly that prefix). No serial console: the first handoff (2026-11-23) stopped at 0.26 s in the 4.1 imx console write, which waits for USR2_TXDC with interrupts off, and the stock suspend had left UART1's clock gated; the stock watchdog reset the board minutes later. The log goes to the Lab126 buffer at 0x9be00000 either way. panic=5, softlockup_panic and hung_task_panic turn a hang the kernel can see into a reboot it does itself, which keeps that log; initcall_debug while the first boots are diagnosed: the second handoff's log stopped after the serial ports with nothing to name the driver it hung in
midr_why: Cortex-A9 r4p1, from the device's /proc/cpuinfo (implementer 0x41, variant 0x4, part 0xc09, revision 1)
prrr_nmrr_why: measured by the first device PROBE (2026-11-23): PRRR 0x000a81a8, NMRR 0x40e040e0, TTBR0 walk attributes 0x59, ACTLR 0xe (SMP bit clear): the SMP_ON_UP kernel found itself on one core and took the UP values, the same as PW3's
forbidden_why: destinations stay in the low 128 MiB; above it are the EPDC reservation (0x9b000000, 3 MiB), the printk buffer (0x9be00000) and the Falcon BIOS (0x9ffc0000-0x9fff0000), which the next kernel needs as the stock one left them
stock_functions_source: sizes: distance to the next text symbol in the device's /proc/kallsyms (80069564, 800229b8, 80021cec); hashes: of those bytes in the device's own memory (readom-probe2 /dev/mem dumps, 2026-11-23), not of a rebuild, whose code differs. The dump's outer_cache has flush_all = 800229b8 and disable = 80021cec and no write_sec, so the L2 is driven from the secure world directly; l2c310_disable tail-calls l2c_disable (800219c4), which is not pinned
